messages:
charlie: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on release/process: what's the concrete release cadence we should plan for next quarter, and what exactly is expected of the oncall during a canary? Also what's the minimum quality bar to start a canary?

nina: Short version: monthly feature releases (target first week), small patch lane weekly for non-emergency fixes, emergency hotfixes on demand. Feature-freeze = 10 days before ship week.

elaine_cto: Canary default for non-security changes. Canary windows usually 12-48h; high-risk or infra/model changes may require staged cohorts. Promote after the agreed monitoring window is stable.

charlie: Which metrics are required to be green before promotion? be specific.

nina: Primary gates: P95 latency <= 1.15x baseline, error-rate delta < 0.1% absolute, CPU/GPU saturation within expected range, and zero new customer-facing regressions in smoke tests. For inference/model changes add eval-set drift < 1% on key prompts. CI smoke and core regression suites must be green.

ops: Is there a written freeze checklist? engineers keep asking which items are mandatory vs nice-to-have.

release-runbook-bot: Runbook (freeze checklist + PR template): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/release-process :link:

nina: Checklist highlights: release notes + reviewers, canary traffic plan (initial % + ramp), rollback plan, perf smoke with representative payloads, QA regression subset green, canary_owner assigned and announced in #eng-oncall, and any SLA routes listed explicitly.

elaine_cto: Oncall handoff rule: the canary_owner listed in the rollout PR is the active responder for the canary window and must post a kickoff in #eng-oncall. For SLA-tagged routes (Dedicated customers) SRE must be CC'd before promoting beyond 20% traffic. We recommend oncall pairing for first 2 hours for risky changes.

charlie: How do we handle flaky tests discovered after canary starts?

nina: If flaky tests affect release signals: pause any promotion, quarantine the test in CI, open a P1 (if metrics are noisy) and aim to triage within 4 hours. If signal ambiguity persists, roll back the canary.

elaine_cto: SLA note: engineering target is to avoid >10% P99 regression on SLA-monitored routes after a release. Legal/ops will confirm contract language, but treat SLA routes as high-sensitivity for canaries.

charlie: Please drop a concrete PR snippet we can paste into rollout PRs.

nina: PR snippet (paste in rollout body):

```
canary_owner: @username
canary_start_utc: 2026-11-02 14:00 UTC
traffic_plan: 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 36h
health_gates: p95_latency, error_rate, infra_saturation, smoke_regressions, model_eval_delta
rollback_plan: revert PR + disable routing; escalate to SRE if SLA routes impacted
sla_routes: [customer/dedicated/*]
smoke_ci_job: <CI job URL>
```

release-runbook-bot: Reminder: update PR template with snippet and link freeze checklist. :memo:

sre-oncall-bot: Reminder: next oncall rotation starts 1965480000.

charlie: Great, i'll post a short summary in the all-hands notes and run a 20min sync for teams with upcoming releases. Thanks all!"
